prompt.context: Assume you are the new pastor of a rural English church in the late nineteenth century. Over the last three years, attendance has been declining. Your boss has just come to town to tell you that she is considering shutting down the church. You have two weeks to diagnose the problem and come up with possible solutions.
prompt.question: How would you think through what these problems might be and the possible solutions?

framework: Diagnose root causes of declining attendance: competitive churches vs. general drop in churchgoing
Test hypotheses through direct research (parishioner interviews, competitor observation, geographic mapping)
Devise an action plan targeting the identified root causes

questions.prompt: What are the possible reasons attendance has been declining?
questions.guidance: Strong answers generate two major hypothesis buckets: (1) Competition from other churches — due to better location, different/more appealing religious doctrine, or superior services offered (childcare, adult education, job training, social events, more personal pastoral attention). (2) People in the area have stopped going to church altogether — driven by scientific/intellectual progress reducing reliance on the church to explain the world, or by economic/convenience constraints (e.g., parishioners need to work the fields and cannot spare time for services).

questions.prompt: How would you test your hypotheses?
questions.guidance: (1) Talk directly to former parishioners to ask why they left and what would bring them back. (2) Visit competing churches during services to observe what is being preached. (3) Draw a map of current and former parishioners to analyze whether distance from the church correlates with lost attendance. (4) Plot competing churches on the same map to assess geographic competition.

questions.prompt: Once you understand the root cause, what solutions would you propose?
questions.guidance: Tailor solutions to root cause: if services are inferior, enhance offerings (e.g., daycare, flexible service times). If location/access is the issue, consider holding services at multiple locations or different times. Focus on the specific needs of the parish rather than generic fixes.

brainstorming.prompt: What specific services or changes could the church offer to attract parishioners back?

categories.name: Service enhancements
ideas: Provide adult education and job training
Host singles dances or social events
Offer more personal attention and guidance from the pastor

categories.name: Accessibility improvements
ideas: Hold services at multiple times of day
Conduct services at different locations closer to parishioner clusters

categories.name: Doctrine/community outreach
ideas: Review and adapt the church's messaging to be more relevant
Reach out personally to lapsed parishioners

recommendation: Interview lapsed parishioners within the first week to identify the primary driver of declining attendance
Based on findings, implement targeted changes: enhance services if competition is the issue, or improve access and scheduling if convenience/economics are the barrier
risks: Changes may not be sufficient if the root cause is a broad cultural shift away from religion
Limited resources (time, money) may constrain the scope of improvements within two weeks
next_steps: Map current and former parishioners geographically alongside competing churches
Visit competitor churches to benchmark their offerings
Present a diagnosis and action plan to the boss at the end of the two-week window
